name: Kerosene wick heater

combustion.note: Rated to burn in a room only with the door open to the rest of the house (plus a window cracked if the door must shut or the house is tight), 1-K fuel and the wick at the maker's height; add a CO alarm. Petrol or petrol-tainted kerosene can turn it into an uncontrollable fire.

comps.spec: Kerosene left in the tank (5.9 L tank on the Toyotomi KS-27A, 7.5 L on the Omni 230). Check it before you burn it: water-clear only, never yellow, cloudy or sour-smelling
comps.loc: Fuel tank in the base, or a lift-out cartridge tank on some models

comps.spec: Fuel tank with a gauge and screw cap: 5.9 L on the Toyotomi KS-27A, 7.5 L on the Omni 230
Squeeze-bulb siphon pump with a vent knob, packed with the KS-27A: moves kerosene from the can into the tank without mouth siphoning
comps.loc: Taped to the heater or in the box

comps.spec: Battery igniter on many models (the Toyotomi Omni 230's is automatic, on four C cells); others, such as the Toyotomi KS-27A, are lit with a match
comps.loc: Beside the wick, behind the lower guard

comps.spec: Cells for the igniter (four C cells in the Omni 230)
comps.loc: Battery box on the side or base

comps.spec: Painted steel cabinet, wire guard and (radiant models) a polished reflector
comps.loc: Outer shell and back of radiant models

comps.spec: Wing nuts and small screws holding the wick adjuster and cover
comps.loc: Around the wick adjuster and cover

buildings.loc: Basement, garage or storage room, often with a can of kerosene nearby
Shelves and corners, with the blue fuel can
Seasonal heating aisle; spare wicks and siphon pumps in the same bay
Heating aisle; kerosene sometimes sold from a pump outside
Workshop, milk house or barn office
Units packed for the cottage or camp

notes: An unvented heater certified to burn indoors (CSA B140.9.3 in Canada, UL 647 in the US) on water-clear 1-K kerosene only, with a door open to the rest of the house, plus a window open about 2.5 cm (1 in) if the door must be shut or the house is tight (CPSC 5052). Even working right it puts carbon monoxide, nitrogen dioxide and sulphur dioxide into the room (MSU E-1669). Toyotomi says substitute wicks can severely reduce performance and safety, and that heater kerosene should be no more than 6 months old (Toyotomi KS-27A).
